items.excerpt: Audiobook publisher Bolinda built an AI voice clone of the late romance author Barbara Cartland, using archival interviews, research and human direction to narrate her backlist. Bolinda staff walk through how consent, estate approval and human oversight were handled.
items.note: On-list (thebookseller.com). Byline date 9 July 2026; freshness.py books -> FRESH. Strong craft/production hook: estate voice licensing + AI narration workflow. Distinct from the 07-16 '17.4% AI narration' stat roundup and the 07-15 AI-audiobook survey — this is a specific production/voice-licensing deal. TBS item 1 of 2.

items.excerpt: Take a Break's Fiction Feast told its regular freelance short-story writers that 'AI tools will be used' on stories produced in-house going forward, raising questions about paid markets for human short fiction.
items.note: On-list (thebookseller.com). article:published_time 10 July 2026; freshness.py books -> FRESH. Direct craft-of-writing hook: a commissioning market swapping freelance human fiction for AI-assisted in-house copy. TBS item 2 of 2.

items.excerpt: A sleuth found that Claude output pasted into Archive of Our Own carried identifying markers, revealing that many fanfics tagged as human-written were in fact LLM-generated — despite strong community opposition to AI.
items.note: On-list (janefriedman.com). Post date 2026-07-15; freshness.py books -> FRESH. Craft/disclosure hook: AI-detection-by-artifact and how writing communities police AI labeling. Fresh sub-angle not covered in the last 2 days.

items.excerpt: Bryan Charles tests ChatGPT against working Proust translators, tracing how AI is quietly encroaching on literary translation — and how skilled translators are actually deploying (and resisting) it.
items.note: On-list (lithub.com). Author-archive + page date 7 July 2026; freshness.py books -> FRESH. Requeried at the craft angle per plan's 'AI literary translation' deprioritization — this is translator-craft, not the 07-16 CONTEC panel or 07-15 Kindle Translate story.

items.excerpt: Three AI startups — Spain's Alighieria (Publisher OS), Germany's Lit-X and New Zealand's Narrative Muse — are pitching publishers on data tools spanning acquisition, trend-spotting and recommendation, promising data-informed decisions without replacing editorial judgment.
items.note: On-list (publishersweekly.com). Dateline 10 July 2026; freshness.py books -> FRESH. Workflow hook: AI entering acquisition/marketing decisions. Adjacent to but distinct from the 07-14 Rakuten discovery and 07-11 pub-data items (different vendors, editorial-acquisition angle). PW item 1 of 2.

items.excerpt: AI dominated the 35th IPA Congress in Kuala Lumpur, with IPA president Gvantsa Jobava framing publishers' catalogues as 'the best source of training data for AI' and keynoter Thad McIlroy saying the trade has moved past the 'golly-gee-whiz phase' into practical implementation.
items.note: On-list (publishersweekly.com). Dateline 6 July 2026; freshness.py books -> FRESH. Industry-craft hook (training-data leverage + adoption posture), not pure business noise. PW item 2 of 2.

items.excerpt: The IPA gave its 2026 Innovation in Publishing Award to two AI companies — Shimmr (AI book marketing) and Ailaysa (multilingual AI for publishers, maker of the Chai Reader discovery platform) — at the Kuala Lumpur congress closing gala.
items.note: On-list (publishingperspectives.com). Published 8 July 2026; freshness.py books -> FRESH. Tool/vendor hook: which AI publishing tools the industry is formally endorsing. PP item 1 of 3.

items.excerpt: An IPA Congress panel on Asian markets examined AI's reshaping of publishing workflows, including the problem of AI-generated books being submitted for legal-deposit compensation in Korea.
items.note: On-list (publishingperspectives.com). Published 10 July 2026; freshness.py books -> FRESH. Includes a Korea-specific AI-flood/legal-deposit angle (matches the plan's 'AI 출판' Korean expansion). PP item 2 of 3.

items.excerpt: The 35th IPA Congress opened in Kuala Lumpur with AI, copyright protection and publishers' role against misinformation as the through-lines of the program.
items.note: On-list (publishingperspectives.com). Published 7 July 2026; freshness.py books -> FRESH. Overlaps the PW IPA item — curator should pick at most one IPA-congress story. PP item 3 of 3 (per-source cap reached).

items.excerpt: A global effort via WCRI/COPE/STM is building a shared 'Vancouver Standard' taxonomy for disclosing AI use in research writing, after a 2026 survey found about a third of researchers have never disclosed their AI use when publishing.
items.note: On-list (scholarlykitchen.sspnet.org). Published 2026-07-13; freshness.py books -> FRESH. Changes how books/papers get written and disclosed — an authorship-labeling standard, on-topic per override #5. SK item 1 of 2.

items.excerpt: Open science must move past access to interpretability, the authors argue: 'Access without interpretability leaves a knowledge system that is formally open but functionally opaque' once AI mediates how readers reach text.
items.note: On-list (scholarlykitchen.sspnet.org). article:published_time 2026-07-14; freshness.py books -> FRESH. Reading/comprehension-layer hook for publishers. Weaker news value than the disclosure-standard piece — backup. SK item 2 of 2.

items.excerpt: The Australian Publishers Association said it is 'encouraged' by government signals on copyright as PM Anthony Albanese prepares to announce an Office of AI within his department, amid pressure from AI firms to loosen text-and-data-mining rules.

items.excerpt: Book Riot's final Today in Books newsletter rounds up the week's publishing news, led by the writer accused of AI use who won the Commonwealth Short Story Prize.
